documentsAndDrawings: Splitsingsplan compliant with Book 5 article 109 Civil Code and applicable apartment-rights decision, showing layout and intended ownership changes, scale at least 1:100.
Building-condition report no older than six months showing that layout/maintenance condition permits splitting or how the building will be adapted.
Foundation report no older than six months showing it is plausible that the foundation will need no maintenance within 25 years.
Gas and electricity inspection report no older than six months from a recognized inspection company showing compliance with Bbl requirements.
If ownership is already divided into apartment rights: proof of VvE consent.
Current/proposed plans and site/access information are part of the broader special application-requirement structure.
For relevant proposed-use cases the plan can require room counts, area information, acoustic isolation plan/report and compensation proposal.
substantiveSplittingRules: Permit can be refused for disproportionate harm to housing-stock composition, liveability, adjacent-land use, residential/living climate or architectural character.
Vertical splitting refused where dwelling ground area excluding outbuildings is under 150 m2 or dwelling volume excluding outbuildings is under 1,000 m3.
Horizontal splitting refused if it is not a social-rental dwelling or if split into more than two units.
